neutral_facts: The accused, along with others, committed a robbery at the house-cum-shop of RL, a money lender. During the robbery, RL and his wife were found dead in a pool of blood. The accused looted the house and fled with the stolen ornaments and cash. The murder weapon, a Jharbad, was recovered from one of the accused and was found stained with human blood. Blood group analysis showed that the blood on the weapon matched the blood group of the deceased. The accused were found in possession of stolen property, including gold ornaments and cash, which were later melted into gold ingots. The prosecution established that the accused had access to the stolen property and that there was no explanation for their possession of the stolen items. The investigation was not tainted, and the evidence of the recovery of the stolen property and the murder weapon was accepted by the courts.
